introduction: These are letters of thanks and of account. Tribute is accepted “as a treasure because it was presented … with all love”; women and children send skeins of their own spinning; a friend is told not to send more because his troubles embarrass the receiver; aid from a troublemaker is refused; ledgers are to be kept complete and certified; sweets, a cloak, an apple, paintbrushes and tiles arrive and are praised; relief goes to refugees; and prayers ask blessing on the givers. Paul’s letters are full of the same business: the willing mind that makes a gift acceptable, Macedonia giving beyond its power, his thanks to Philippi for “an odour of a sweet smell”, witnesses travelling with the collection “providing for honest things … in the sight of men”. The tabernacle was built from offerings until there was more than enough. The cautions are the Gospel’s secret alms, Emerson’s remark that we do not quite forgive a giver, and the Qur’an’s givers who want no thanks.
questions: “If there be first a willing mind, it is accepted.” How do readings 1 to 10 decide what makes a gift acceptable, and when one should be declined?
The Right of God is called obligatory, yet it may not be solicited. How does Paul’s “not grudgingly, or of necessity” illuminate that combination?
Jesus asks that alms be secret; these letters name givers and amounts. What purposes does acknowledgment serve that secrecy would not, and what dangers does it carry?
Paul provided “for honest things … in the sight of men”. Why do readings 127 to 130 care so much about receipts and ledgers?
Emerson says a gift can wound the receiver’s independence. How does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, as a receiver, protect both the giver’s dignity and his own (32, 155 to 157)?

outside.why: The tribute is accepted “as a treasure because it was presented … with all love”. If there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not.
The measure in the Gospel is the same: this poor widow hath cast in more than they all, for she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.

Nothing in the world is worthy of mention, yet what a soul offers in God’s path is. When Israel gave for the temple, the people rejoiced, for that they offered willingly, because with perfect heart they offered willingly to the Lord.
An accepted offering was returned twofold. Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over.
Skeins and weavings sent by women and children are “spiritual treasure”. She hath done what she could.
For the tabernacle they came, every one whose heart stirred him up, and brought the Lord’s offering; and the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands.

Affection is the reason a gift from old friends is accepted. Paul acknowledging a gift from Philippi: I have all, and abound, having received the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable.
Trade conducted for the sake of God prospers. Honour the Lord with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase: so shall thy barns be filled with plenty.
Payment of the Right of God is obligatory, and its benefit returns to the giver. Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, and prove me now herewith, if I will not open you the windows of heaven.

Yet its acceptance depends on the spirit in which it is given, and it may not be demanded. Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver. How can something be an obligation and never be asked for?
One friend gives beyond his means. Of the churches of Macedonia: their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality; beyond their power they were willing of themselves.
“I am very embarrassed by his troubles and am absolutely not willing for him to send” more. Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
Emerson on the awkwardness of gifts: we do not quite forgive a giver; the hand that feeds us is in some danger of being bitten. The readings handle that danger from the receiver’s side. How?
Property is not to be sold to pay the Right of God. Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?
Aid offered by one who seeks to mislead is refused. Peter to Simon the sorcerer: thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

If nothing was sent to each by name, “this was due to wisdom”. Much of this guide consists of naming and thanking givers. Jesus: when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth, that thine alms may be in secret. What is the difference between acknowledging a gift and publishing it?
Do not hurry to sell land for the Cause. Proverbs prefers prudence in one’s affairs: seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.
A loan to a fellow believer is counted a service. He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
A family hosted travellers generously. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
“Praise be to God that thou hast been enabled to discharge thy debts.” Owe no man any thing, but to love one another.
Services rendered during a stay are remembered and thanked. We have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
A rosewater sprinkler is brought, used, and its giver mentioned. The house was filled with the odour of the ointment.
A trifle is sent in return, “that thou mayest know of My” remembrance. Whosoever shall give a cup of cold water only shall in no wise lose his reward.
Pages in the Báb’s handwriting are received as a gift. Paul’s one request for things: the cloke, and the books, but especially the parchments.
A sum submitted “with the utmost joy”. Remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Everything sent through each agent is listed. Paul, carrying a collection, travels with witnesses: providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
“Keep the account book complete, organized and certified.” It is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
Small sums are reported one by one. He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
A ledger of contributions for the oppressed of Nayríz. The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea.
Tea “suited for princes rather than for prisoners”. The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

A fine cloak is praised and its love acknowledged. When a woman spent costly ointment on Jesus some asked, why was this waste? and he defended her. When should a costly gift be received as love and not declined as excess?
A hundred tiles of new design are offered for a holy building. The craftsmen of the tabernacle had to tell Moses: the people bring much more than enough for the service of the work.
“These sweets have no equal, for they were sent with utmost love.” Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.
Support for a school merits the highest praise. Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
A share of an inheritance is dedicated to a house of worship. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts.
Write down the names of those who took part. Rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.
A monthly sum is assigned for one in need. The tithe is laid up within thy gates, that the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow may come, and eat and be satisfied.
He is pleased with one who helped clear a society’s debt. Paul: it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.
“Despite straitened circumstances” he too contributes. Ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor.

Money for the survivors of martyrs and for refugees. If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, and one say, Be ye warmed and filled, and give them not those things which are needful, what doth it profit?
Paul’s principle for relief between churches: that now at this time your abundance may be a supply for their want, that there may be equality.
A prayer for blessing on the homes of those who gave. The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: the Lord make his face shine upon thee.

“Accept from them this charitable contribution and increase … their wealth.” The likeness of those who spend their wealth in God’s way is as a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains.
Whatever has been shown in the path of God has been accepted. God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love.

He expresses boundless gratitude for the friends’ affection in prison. The Qur’an’s ideal givers say: we feed you for the sake of God only; we wish for no reward nor thanks from you. What does a receiver’s thanks add to a gift that sought none?

shortfall: Most of these hundred readings are brief acknowledgments of particular sums and objects, with names, dates and instructions; they have companions for the principles they show (the willing mind, the right to decline, careful accounts, relief of the needy, thanks) and not one each.
